comments.text:
Which part of Congo stayed with you the most — the river acting as a road, the 220+ meter depth, Goma beneath Nyiragongo, the bonobos and okapi, or the cobalt connection to modern technology?

I’d especially like to know which discovery changed the way you pictured the Democratic Republic of the Congo before watching.

If you enjoyed this journey, continue exploring some of the world’s most extraordinary places with us:

Living in Vanuatu https://youtu.be/00Wc0J7_u-M
Living in Samoa https://youtu.be/wMZBPAeZ2do

Which place should we explore next? 🌍

comments.author: @TravelAcrossEarth68
comments.text: The Congo River isn’t just a river—it’s a highway, a lifeline, and sometimes the only road people have. 🌍🚤 It makes you wonder what daily life looks like when water connects places that roads simply can’t reach.

replies.author: @BestHiddenPlaces
replies.text: Absolutely! The Congo River plays such an important role in everyday life, connecting communities and carrying people and goods across vast distances. It’s fascinating to see how people adapt when the river becomes their main road. Thanks for sharing your thoughts!
